svg.title: Landmark findings in the history of cognitive psychology
svg.desc: A vertical timeline of nine landmark findings from 1879 to 2015: Wundt's Leipzig laboratory, Bartlett's reconstructive memory, Miller's chunks, Hubel and Wiesel's orientation-selective neurons, Neisser's book, Shepard and Metzler's mental rotation, Gick and Holyoak's analogy study, Kanwisher and colleagues' face-responsive region, and the Open Science Collaboration's replication project. Years are dates of publication or of the work described. Summaries, not a complete history.

g.text: Wundt opens an experimental laboratory at Leipzig
Bartlett: remembered stories are rebuilt from prior knowledge
Miller: short-term capacity described in chunks
Hubel and Wiesel: single neurons tuned to edge orientation
Neisser's Cognitive Psychology gives the field its scope
Shepard and Metzler: time to match rotated objects grows with angle
Gick and Holyoak: analogies used once their relevance is pointed out
Kanwisher and colleagues: face-responsive region of the fusiform gyrus
Open Science Collaboration: 100 replications, weaker effects

svg.text: Years are dates of publication or of the work described. Entries are summaries, not a complete history.
